title: A Turning Point for Hong Kong

sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的

sentences.zh: 商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的舞台上，

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: New security law is bringing China's harsh approach to free speech to Hong Kong in an attempt to stamp out protests there.
sentences.zh: 新的国家安全法将中国对言论自由的严厉态度引入香港，试图扑灭那里的抗议活动。

sentences.en: My colleague, Austin Ramsey, on The Fallout.
sentences.zh: 我的同事奥斯汀·拉姆齐带来关于其余波的报道。

sentences.en: Monday, July 13th.
sentences.zh: 7 月 13 日，星期一。

sentences.en: Austin, when did you first start to hear about this new security law in Hong Kong?
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀，你是什么时候第一次听说香港这部新安全法的？

sentences.en: I first heard about it in mid-May.
sentences.zh: 我是在五月中旬第一次听说的。

sentences.en: I was going to work one morning.
sentences.zh: 那天早上我正要去上班。

sentences.en: I was outside the subway station in the neighborhood where I live on Hong Kong Island called Wan Chai.
sentences.zh: 我在港岛湾仔我住的社区的地铁站外面。

sentences.en: It's a really crowded part of town.
sentences.zh: 那是城里非常拥挤的一个地方。

sentences.en: And as I was passing into the station, I noticed a petition booth.
sentences.zh: 当我走进地铁站时，我注意到一个请愿摊位。

sentences.en: And they were collecting signatures for something called
sentences.zh: 他们正在为一个名为

sentences.en: Article 23, which was a security law that the Hong Kong government had tried and failed to pass 17 years ago.
sentences.zh: “第 23 条”的事项收集签名，这是一项香港政府在 17 年前曾试图通过但未能成功的安全法。

sentences.en: And when you say security law, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 当你说是安全法时，你指的是什么？

sentences.en: It was a law that outlawed things like secession and subversion.
sentences.zh: 这是一项将分裂国家和颠覆国家政权等行为定为非法的法律。

sentences.en: But people worried that it was so broad that it could outlaw all sorts of behavior in Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 但人们担心它的范围如此之广，可能会将香港的各种行为都定为非法。

sentences.en: And so people took to the streets and there was a mass protest on July 1st,
sentences.zh: 于是人们走上街头，在 2003 年
7 月 1 日爆发了大规模抗议。

sentences.en: And shortly after that, the government backed down and has never picked up the law since.
sentences.zh: 在那之后不久，政府做出了妥协，此后再也没有提及这部法律。

sentences.en: So when you see this idea reemerge of a security law on your way into the subway, what are you thinking?
sentences.zh: 所以当你走去地铁站的路上再次看到安全法这个概念时，你在想什么？

sentences.en: It was a sense of disbelief, really.
sentences.zh: 其实是一种难以置信的感觉。

sentences.en: I mean, it's something that's sort of part of the political environment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是某种属于政治环境一部分的东西。

sentences.en: It sort of comes up from time to time.
sentences.zh: 它有时会浮现出来。

sentences.en: But everyone sort of says, no, it's not possible.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都会说，不，这不可能。

sentences.en: There's no way the government can push this through.
sentences.zh: 政府绝不可能强行通过这个。

sentences.en: And certainly not now, after a year of the most intense protests Hong Kong has ever seen.
sentences.zh: 当然绝不是现在，在经历了香港有史以来最激烈的抗议活动一年之后。

sentences.en: Things were dying down a little bit with the coronavirus and police sort of being more aggressive.
sentences.zh: 随着新冠疫情的爆发以及警方表现得更加咄咄逼人，局势稍微平静了一些。

sentences.en: It seemed like the government sort of had the protesters on the back foot.
sentences.zh: 看起来政府似乎把抗议者逼到了守势。

sentences.en: And so the idea that they would do something that would encourage people to come out again in mass numbers, it just seemed inconceivable to me.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们会做出一件会鼓励人们再次大规模走上街头的事情，这在我看来简直是不可思议的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Okay, so what ends up happening next?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So a few weeks later, China's Congress meets in Beijing.
sentences.zh: 所以几周后，中国的全国人大在北京开会。

sentences.en: A friend and I were discussing going out for drinks on the night that the Congress starts.
sentences.zh: 我和一个朋友在人大开幕的那天晚上讨论去喝一杯。

sentences.en: And my friend, who's a former China correspondent, said, are you sure you won't be busy on the start of the National People's Congress?
sentences.zh: 我的朋友是一位前中国问题记者，他说：“你确定你在全国人大开幕那天不忙吗？”

sentences.en: And I said, of course, there's nothing that's going to affect Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 我说：“当然不忙，没有什么会影响到香港的。”

sentences.en: And then it emerged that the National People's Congress planned to pass a security law for Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 然后有消息称，全国人大计划为香港通过一项安全法。

sentences.en: It's a shock to everyone in the city.
sentences.zh: 这对全城的每个人来说都是一个震撼。

sentences.en: It really emerges out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 它真的是毫无征兆地出现了。

sentences.en: So a security law, it sounds like, very much like what you saw a petition for in your neighborhood a few weeks before.
sentences.zh: 所以安全法听起来，非常类似于你几周前在你的社区看到别人请愿的那部法律。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Very much like the security law that the Hong Kong government had tried to pass for
sentences.zh: 非常类似于香港政府试图通过了

sentences.en: 17 years and never succeeded.
sentences.zh: 17 年却从未成功的安全法。

sentences.en: Austin, how exactly can China do that?
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀，中国怎么能这样做呢？

sentences.en: Pass a law that regulates Hong Kong that, from what you're saying, Hong Kong does not want for itself.
sentences.zh: 通过一项监管香港的法律，而从你所说的情况来看，香港并不想要它。

sentences.en: It's rejected it.
sentences.zh: 香港已经拒绝了它。

sentences.en: Because my sense is that
sentences.zh: 因为我的印象是

sentences.en: Hong Kong has its own legislature and retains a fair bit of independence from China.
sentences.zh: 香港拥有自己的立法机关，并保留了相当大程度的对华独立性。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Hong Kong is a former British colony returned to Chinese control in 1997.
sentences.zh: 所以香港是一个前英国殖民地，于 1997 年回归中国管治。

sentences.en: And under what's called one country, two systems, it is supposed to operate with a high degree of autonomy for 50 years after that.
sentences.zh: 根据所谓的“一国两制”，它本应在此后的 50 年里保持高度自治。

sentences.en: And so by China's legislature passing a law like this, in 2020, it's acting way ahead of schedule and doing something that it's not really supposed to do until 2047.
sentences.zh: 因此，中国立法机关在 2020 年通过这样一部法律，完全是超前行事，做了一件本不应该在 2047 年之前做的事情。

sentences.en: So this is not how this is supposed to work.
sentences.zh: 所以事情本不该是这样的。

sentences.en: China crafting laws that directly govern Hong Kong's freedoMs.
sentences.zh: 中国起草直接管理香港自由的法律。

sentences.en: No, that's not how it's supposed to work.
sentences.zh: 不，事情本不该是这样的。

sentences.en: And Austin, what does this law actually do?
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀，这部法律实际上做了什么？

sentences.en: What does it actually say?
sentences.zh: 它究竟写了什么？

sentences.en: Well, nobody knows exactly because at that point, the law has not been written.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有人确切知道，因为在那时，法律还没有被撰写出来。

sentences.en: It's a brief outline
sentences.zh: 这只是一个简短的轮廓

sentences.en: authorizing the Chinese government to write this law.
sentences.zh: 授权中国政府来撰写这部法律。

sentences.en: And so it targets secession, subversion,
sentences.zh: 因此它的目标是分裂国家、颠覆国家政权、

sentences.en: terrorist activities, and collusion with foreign powers.
sentences.zh: 恐怖活动以及勾结外国势力。

sentences.en: But we're all left to wonder what exactly those words mean, what exactly the Chinese government has in store for Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 但我们所有人都只能去猜测这些词究竟意味着什么，中国政府究竟为香港准备了什么。

sentences.en: And I'm curious, what is the government and the leadership in Hong Kong saying after Beijing says it's going to be writing this law?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，在北京宣布将起草这部法律后，香港的政府和领导层是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Are they filling in the gaps here?
sentences.zh: 他们有在填补这些空白吗？

sentences.en: Are they just as confused as you are?
sentences.zh: 他们和你们一样迷惑吗？

sentences.en: Well, the first thing they say is that this is very welcome.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们说的第一件事是这非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: This is exactly what Hong Kong needs.
sentences.zh: 这正是香港所需要的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This will help with all the problems we've been facing, the unrest and the violence on the streets.
sentences.zh: 这将有助于解决我们一直面临的所有问题，即街头的动乱和暴力。

sentences.en: But when pressed on what exactly the law will say, they have to acknowledge that they don't know.
sentences.zh: 但当被追问法律具体会怎么写时，他们不得不承认他们不知道。

sentences.en: So at one point, Kiri Lam, the chief executive of Hong Kong, the top official here, has asked about this.
sentences.zh: 因此在某个时刻，香港特首、这里最高官员林郑月娥被问及此事。

sentences.en: Why should people take your comments and your minister's comments about the national security law seriously, if you guys have not read details in the clauses?
sentences.zh: “如果你们还没有阅读条款的细节，为什么人们要认真对待你和你的部长们关于国家安全法的评论呢？”

sentences.en: Thank you for those questions.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的这些问题。

sentences.en: Well, first, yes, you are right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，是的，你说得对。

sentences.en: We have not seen the complete details of the proposed legislation.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有看到拟议立法的完整细节。

sentences.en: We were commenting on what we have seen.
sentences.zh: 我们是在对我们已经看到的内容进行评论。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And there was this published by the Xinhua News Agency, which contains actually quite a lot of details.
sentences.zh: 新华社发布了这一内容，其中实际上包含了相当多的细节。

sentences.en: So even Kiri Lam, someone who's seen as a very pro-Beijing figure, she is sort of caught like a deer
sentences.zh: 所以即使是林郑月娥这样被视为非常亲北京的人物，她也像是被强光照到的鹿一样

sentences.en: in headlights and trying to defend the law at the same time, acknowledging that she doesn't know exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 不知所措，在试图为法律辩护的同时，承认她并不知道具体内容是什么。

sentences.en: So based on that, I have given you my comments and my understanding.
sentences.zh: 因此基于此，我向你们给出了我的评论和理解。

sentences.en: So I have to imagine that the citizens of Hong Kong are deeply skeptical and worried about this law and not following their leader's advice to blindly support it.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不想象，香港市民对这部法律深表怀疑和担忧，并没有听从他们领导人的建议盲目支持它。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People are very worried about the law.
sentences.zh: 人们对这部法律非常担心。

sentences.en: At the same time, that lack of clarity paralyzes people because this law is something that targets dissent.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，缺乏透明度让人们陷入瘫痪，因为这部法律针对的是异见。

sentences.en: And people grow very worried that anything they do or say could be made a crime under this law.
sentences.zh: 人们变得非常担心，他们所做的或说的任何事情在这部法律下都可能构成犯罪。

sentences.en: And so you begin to see people deleting social media accounts and becoming very worried about things they might say that could later come back to haunt them under this new law.
sentences.zh: 于是你开始看到人们删除社交媒体账号，并对他们可能说过的话感到非常担忧，这些话日后可能会在新法下成为他们的把柄。

sentences.en: That makes me wonder if China understood that the ambiguity of this all, you know, authorizing a law,
sentences.zh: 这让我不禁想知道，中国是否明白这种含糊不清的做法——你知道，授权一部法律，

sentences.en: but not necessarily explaining what would be in it, using words like sedition and terrorism, but not defining them, if that was deliberate.
sentences.zh: 但不一定解释其中会包含什么，使用煽动叛乱和恐怖主义等词汇却不加定义——是否是蓄意为之的。

sentences.en: Yes, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: In fact, there were some officials who make this clear that this ambiguity is by design and it's basically meant to intimidate people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些官员明确表示这种模棱两可的设计是刻意为之的，其主要目的是恐吓人们。

sentences.en: Friends from the press, good morning.
sentences.zh: 各位新闻界的朋友，大家早上好。

sentences.en: One of them, a man named Zhang Xiaoming, gives a press conference on the law and he gives a stern warning that it's not something you want to mess with.
sentences.zh: 其中一位名叫张晓明的人就该法律举行了新闻发布会，并发出严厉警告，称这不是你可以胡来的东西。

sentences.en: If those in Hong Kong who defy and challenge the authority of the central government and undermine stability in Hong Kong are allowed to have their way,
sentences.zh: 如果香港那些公然挑战中央政府权威、破坏香港稳定的人能够为所欲为，

sentences.en: Hong Kong would be the loser.
sentences.zh: 香港将是输家。

sentences.en: There is no doubt to that.
sentences.zh: 这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: And then he says something really striking to me.
sentences.zh: 然后他说了一句让我觉得非常震撼的话。

sentences.en: This law will be
sentences.zh: 这部法律将

sentences.en: the sword of Damocles hanging over a tiny group of criminals who endanger national security, who interfere in Hong Kong affairs.
sentences.zh: 是高悬在极少数危害国家安全、干预香港事务的罪犯头顶的达摩克利斯之剑。

sentences.en: He says that the law is like the sword of Damocles hanging over Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 他说这部法律就像是悬在香港头顶的达摩克利斯之剑。

sentences.en: The sword of Damocles is a mythological tale about a man who wants to be king and the king agrees to allow him to sit on the throne.
sentences.zh: 达摩克利斯之剑是一个神话故事，讲述了一个渴望成为国王的人，国王同意让他坐在王座上。

sentences.en: But as part of the agreement, there's a sword that's hanging above him from a single horse's hair.
sentences.zh: 但作为协议的一部分，有一把剑用一根马鬃悬在他的头顶上方。

sentences.en: And the man is so frightened that the sword will fall on him that he begs to no longer be on the throne.
sentences.zh: 这个人吓得生怕剑落下来，于是乞求不要再坐在王座上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because at any moment that horse hair can break and the sword will fall.
sentences.zh: 因为在任何时刻那根马鬃都可能断裂，剑就会落下来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Which is no way to be king.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是当国王的方法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The idea is that it's such a miserable experience that that no one would want it to happen to them.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，这是一种如此痛苦的经历，以至于没有人会希望它发生在自己身上。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So as this parable applies to Hong Kong, if I have this correct,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这个寓意适用于香港，如果我理解得没错的话，

sentences.en: Damocles is the people of Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 达摩克利斯就是香港人民。

sentences.en: The king is China.
sentences.zh: 国王就是中国。

sentences.en: And the sword is this ambiguous security law that makes everything feel precarious and has everyone living in a certain amount of fear.
sentences.zh: 而这把剑就是这部模棱两可的安全法，它让一切都显得岌岌可危，让每个人都生活在一定程度的恐惧之中。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's this sense of fear that in this place that's known for its free speech, suddenly anything you say could potentially be used against you
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧感在于，在这个以言论自由闻名的地方，突然之间你说的任何话都可能被用来对付你，

sentences.en: and you could potentially end up in prison.
sentences.zh: 而你最终可能会入狱。

sentences.en: And that is what's hanging over Hong Kong so precariously.
sentences.zh: 这就是悬在香港头上、如此岌岌可危的东西。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 解锁《纽约时报》App。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在该App中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订户每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订户，请立即下载《时报》App并获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Austin, when does it finally become clear precisely what this national security law actually says and does?
sentences.zh: 那么，奥斯汀，这部国家安全法究竟写了什么、做了什么，是什么时候才最终明朗的？

sentences.en: Well, the language of the national security law only becomes clear when it's released.
sentences.zh: 嗯，国家安全法的文本只有在发布时才明朗。

sentences.en: Nobody knows exactly when it's going to come out.
sentences.zh: 没有人确切知道它什么时候会公布。

sentences.en: People are looking at the government website and waiting, waiting, checking.
sentences.zh: 人们一直在查看政府网站并等待、等待、不断刷新。

sentences.en: And then finally, at about 11 p.m., the night of June 30th, it lands.
sentences.zh: 然后终于在大约晚上 11 点，即 6 月 30 日的夜晚，它落地了。

sentences.en: And when it lands, and I assume you're one of those people checking the website over and over again, what does it actually say?
sentences.zh: 当它落地时——我猜你就是那些一遍又一遍刷新网站的人之一——它究竟写了什么？

sentences.en: What's the wording?
sentences.zh: 具体的措辞是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's quite long.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它相当长。

sentences.en: It's 66 articles and six sections.
sentences.zh: 有 66 条，分为六章。

sentences.en: And as it starts out, it describes the law as something that's meant to uphold one country, two systeMs.
sentences.zh: 在开头部分，它将这部法律描述为旨在维护“一国两制”的事物。

sentences.en: But as I read through it, it becomes clear that the law undermines that.
sentences.zh: 但当我通读它时，很明显这部法律实际上破坏了这一点。

sentences.en: Because in these 66 articles, it begins to define the words that have been hanging over Hong Kong for weeks.
sentences.zh: 因为在这 66 条中，它开始界定那些已经在香港头顶悬了数周之久的词汇。

sentences.en: It's secession, subversion, terrorism, collusion with foreign powers, all things that have been criminalized under this new law.
sentences.zh: 这就是分裂国家、颠覆国家政权、恐怖主义、勾结外国势力，所有这些都在这项新法律下被定为刑事犯罪。

sentences.en: So let me just read one of these definitions, subversion.
sentences.zh: 所以让我来读一下其中的一个定义，颠覆。

sentences.en: Subversion, it says, is, quote, a person who undermines the basic system of the People's Republic of China, overthrowing the central power of the People's Republic of China,
sentences.zh: 颠覆，上面说，引述，是指一个人破坏中华人民共和国的基本制度，推翻中华人民共和国中央政权，

sentences.en: or the body of power in Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 或是香港的政权机关。

sentences.en: It goes on to define subversion as, quote, seriously interfering in, disrupting, or undermining the performance of duties and functions in accordance with the law
sentences.zh: 它接着将颠覆定义为，引述，严重干扰、阻挠或破坏中华人民共和国或香港特别行政区

sentences.en: by the body of power of the People's Republic of China or the Hong Kong special administrative region.
sentences.zh: 政权机关依法履行职责和职能。

sentences.en: Those words, interfering, disrupting, undermining, that feels pretty broad.
sentences.zh: 那些词，干扰、阻挠、破坏，听起来相当宽泛。

sentences.en: It feels like a lot of activities could be construed as falling under those words.
sentences.zh: 感觉很多活动都可以被解释为落入这些词的范畴。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And many of the activities that took place, protests over the past year, could fall under those words.
sentences.zh: 而过去一年中发生的许多活动，即抗议活动，都可能落入这些词的范畴。

sentences.en: And so once this law goes into effect, and scary words like subversion are now being defined,
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦这项法律生效，像颠覆这样可怕的词现在被定义了，

sentences.en: and defined in ways that, if I lived in Hong Kong, would make me think that any challenge to authority might suddenly be illegal.
sentences.zh: 而且这种定义方式，如果我住在香港，会让我觉得对权威的任何挑战都可能突然变得非法。

sentences.en: What ends up happening on the streets?
sentences.zh: 街头最终会发生什么？

sentences.en: So the law goes into effect at 11 p.m.
sentences.zh: 所以这部法律在6月30日晚上11点生效，然后一个小时后，就是7月1日。

sentences.en: on June 30th, and then an hour later, it's July 1St.
sentences.zh: 这是一个惊人的时间点，因为7月1日是一个国定假日。

sentences.en: And that's astonishing timing, because July 1st is a national holiday.
sentences.zh: 这是香港非常重要的一天。

sentences.en: It's a very important day in Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 这是香港从英国移交给中国的一天。

sentences.en: It's the day that Hong Kong was handed back from Britain to China.
sentences.zh: 这也成了一个抗议的日子。

sentences.en: It's also become a day of proteSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，导致第一部安全法被搁置的那场最初的抗议活动就发生在2003年7月1日。

sentences.en: In fact, the original protest that led to the first security law being blocked happened on July 1st, 2003.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，每年的这一天都会有抗议活动。

sentences.en: And every year since then, there have been protests on this day.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 所以这部可能使抗议变得更加危险的法律，在这个抗议日的前夜发布了。

sentences.en: So this law that could make protesting far more dangerous has been released the night before this day of proteSt.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 这是一种巧合吗？

sentences.en: And is that a coincidence?
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不觉得这是巧合。

sentences.en: I don't think it's a coincidence at all.
sentences.zh: 在最后一刻抛出这个，其目的就是制造不确定性。

sentences.en: By dropping this at the 11th hour, it's intended to create uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 人们在7月1日醒来，决定是否要去抗议。

sentences.en: People are waking up on July 1st, deciding whether they want to go proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这部法律已经生效，这给走上街头的人带来了巨大的风险感。

sentences.en: They know this law is in effect, and it creates a great sense of risk for people going out on the street.
sentences.zh: 所以在7月1日的早晨，你做了什么，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: So on the morning of July 1st, what do you do, and what do you see?
sentences.zh: 所以我起得很早，走到海滨去搭出租车，我注意到这艘驳船上写着巨大的字，20英尺高，红底黄字，上面写着，

sentences.en: So I got up early, I went out to catch a cab by the waterfront, and I noticed this barge with these huge characters, 20 feet high, yellow on red that said,
sentences.zh: 庆祝香港国安法。

sentences.en: celebrate the national security law.
sentences.zh: 这艘驳船被拖过香港市中心的维多利亚港，你在两岸都能看到，这些巨大的字欢迎着新的国安法。

sentences.en: And this barge was towed through Victoria Harbor in the middle of Hong Kong, and you could see it from either side, these huge characters welcoming the new security law.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常让人联想起中国宣传风格的东西。

sentences.en: And this is something that is a style that is very much reminiscent of Chinese propaganda.
sentences.zh: 现在它出现在香港的市中心。

sentences.en: Now it's in the middle of Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 然后我到达了铜锣湾这个社区，每年的7月1日游行通常都是从这里开始的。

sentences.en: And then I arrived at this neighborhood, Causeway Bay, where every year the protest march on July 1st usually begins.
sentences.zh: 我立刻看到那里聚集了大量人群。

sentences.en: And right away I could see there was a large crowd.
sentences.zh: 有点很难分清谁是谁，因为这是一个购物区，又是假期，有很多人出来。

sentences.en: It was sort of hard to tell who was who, because it's a shopping neighborhood, it's a holiday, there's lots of people out.
sentences.zh: 但很快就很明显，街上到处都是抗议者。

sentences.en: But it becomes quickly clear that there are protesters out everywhere on the streets.
sentences.zh: 我可以看到警察试图封锁铜锣湾的部分街道，能听到人们向警察大喊，

sentences.en: I can see police who are trying to block off parts of the streets in Causeway Bay, can hear people shouting at police,
sentences.zh: 能看到警员举起一面紫色的横幅，告诉人们他们违反了新的国安法。

sentences.en: can see police officers raising a purple banner that tells people that they are in violation of the new security law.
sentences.zh: 紫色横幅上写着什么？

sentences.en: What does the purple banner say?
sentences.zh: 它相当长。

sentences.en: It's quite lengthy.
sentences.zh: 就像是一条写满密密麻麻小字的横幅。

sentences.en: And it's like a fine print banner.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，这是警方警告。

sentences.en: It says, this is a police warning.
sentences.zh: 你们正在展示旗帜或横幅或高喊口号或进行具有分裂或颠覆等意图的行为，

sentences.en: You are displaying flags or banners or chanting slogans or conducting yourself with an intent such as secession or subversion,
sentences.zh: 这可能构成违反香港国安法的罪行。

sentences.en: which may constitute offenses under the Hong Kong national security law.
sentences.zh: 这基本上表明，警方现在将开始对言论进行管控和监察。

sentences.en: It's basically showing that the police will now be out policing words, policing language.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So what happens next?
sentences.zh: 警察开始向这些抗议者靠拢。

sentences.en: Police begin closing in on these protesters.
sentences.zh: 他们对一些人喷胡椒喷雾，并开始在这项新法律下进行首批逮捕。

sentences.en: They pepper spray some people and they begin making the first arrests under this new law.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布在国安法下已经进行了第一起逮捕。

sentences.en: They announce that the first arrest has been made under the national security law.
sentences.zh: 他们称他们拦下一名男子并进行了搜查，在他的包里发现了一面香港独立旗。

sentences.en: They say that they stopped and searched a man and in his bag they found a Hong Kong independence flag.
sentences.zh: 而他甚至还没有把旗帜展示出来。

sentences.en: And he hadn't even displayed the flag.
sentences.zh: 他只是把它放在包里，警察搜查时发现了它。

sentences.en: He had just had it in his bag and police found it when they searched him.
sentences.zh: 这真的很像是思想警察，因为展开的旗帜是未表达的思想。

sentences.en: That very much does feel like the thought police, because a flag unfurled is a thought unexpressed.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像现在的法律规定，甚至只是想一想某事，甚至都没有说出来，都可能触犯法律。

sentences.en: And it's almost as if this law now says that even thinking something, not even saying it, can be a violation of the law.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 在香港，这个拥有亚洲最强健言论自由保障之一的城市，突然发生了这种情况，

sentences.en: And in Hong Kong, a city that had some of the most robust protections for free speech in Asia, to suddenly have this happen,
sentences.zh: 人们因为拥有的文字而被捕。

sentences.en: people are being arrested for words in their possession.
sentences.zh: 这对这里的人们来说是一个真正的冲击。

sentences.en: It's a real shock to people here.
sentences.zh: 那么7月1日是如何结束的？

sentences.en: So how does July 1st come to an end?
sentences.zh: 抗议活动整个下午都在持续。

sentences.en: So protests continue throughout the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 到一天结束时，警方已逮捕了370人，其中10人在新的国安法下被捕。

sentences.en: By the end of the day, the police have arrested 370 people, including 10 under the new national security laws.
sentences.zh: 其中一人是一名15岁的女孩，她和那个男子一样，手里挥舞着一面香港独立旗。

sentences.en: One of them is a 15-year-old girl who, like that man, had a Hong Kong independence flag that she was waving.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他们逮捕了他，一个孩子。

sentences.en: So basically, they arrest him, a child.
sentences.zh: 一个孩子。

sentences.en: A child.
sentences.zh: 在你看来，这项法律是否正在实现它的明显目标，即压制言论自由，并将对中国的异见限制在香港境内？

sentences.en: Does it feel to you that this law is accomplishing what it very much seems its goal is, which is to repress free speech and keep dissent against China contained in Hong Kong?
sentences.zh: 是的，你已经可以看到这部法律的影响了。

sentences.en: Yes, you can already see the effects of this law.
sentences.zh: 整个城市里，有许多支持抗议运动的餐馆和咖啡馆，它们通常贴满标语和横幅之类的东西。

sentences.en: Throughout the city, there are a number of restaurants and cafes that support the protest movement that are normally covered in signs and banners and stuff.
sentences.zh: 其中许多店已经把这些东西取下了，他们的墙壁现在空空如也。

sentences.en: And many of them have taken those down and their walls are now bare.
sentences.zh: 有知情人联系我，要求我删除与他们的聊天记录。

sentences.en: Sources have contacted me and asked that I delete a messaging history with them.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 现在，有时当你向人们征求评论或采访时，那些平时很乐意交谈的人会说，现在不行，

sentences.en: And now, sometimes, when you ask people for comments or interview, people who would normally be very willing to talk say, not right now,
sentences.zh: 他们担心法律问题，根本无法开口。

sentences.en: that they're worried about the law and they just can't talk.
sentences.zh: 所以人们真的担心他们与你的交流可能会违反这些法律。

sentences.en: So people actually worry that their communications with you may violate these laws.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 他们担心，你知道，不仅是他们可能会在公开场合说出一些会惹上麻烦的话，

sentences.en: They're worried either that, you know, not just that they might say something on the record that could get them in trouble,
sentences.zh: 而且我们在过去某个时候分享的一些私人信息可能会让他们入罪。

sentences.en: but that some sort of private message that we shared at some point in the past could incriminate them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正试图删除所有这些。

sentences.en: And so they're trying to delete all of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想起了我们在对话开始时你所说的话，香港人觉得他们还有时间，

sentences.en: You know, I'm reminded of what you said at the beginning of our conversation, that the people of Hong Kong felt that they had time,
sentences.zh: 他们还有几十年的时间，直到这种变化从中国内地传过来。

sentences.en: that they had decades until this kind of a change was going to come from mainland China.
sentences.zh: 所以我纳闷，人们是否开始觉得他们被剥夺了大量的时间，来成为他们一直以来所是的那些人，

sentences.en: And so I wonder if it's starting to feel like people are being robbed of a big chunk of time to be what they have been
sentences.zh: 以及他们认为自己在香港应该被允许成为的人。

sentences.en: and what they think they're supposed to be allowed to be in Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 我认为在香港，一直有一种感觉，即让这个城市独一无二的东西总是受到威胁，并且一直在逐渐消失。

sentences.en: I think in Hong Kong, there's always this sense that what makes the city unique is always under threat and has always been gradually disappearing.
sentences.zh: 但那本应是一个缓慢的过程，年复一年，香港会失去一点点，

sentences.en: But that it would have been a slow process and year by year, Hong Kong would lose a little bit
sentences.zh: 直到2047年，你将无法看出它与中国其他地方有什么区别。

sentences.en: to the point where by 2047, you couldn't tell the difference from the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 但现在感觉这个过程被疯狂地加速了。

sentences.en: But now it feels like that process has accelerated wildly.
sentences.zh: 所以在短短的几周内，我们已经失去了几十年的时间。

sentences.en: And so in a matter of a couple of weeks, we have lost decades.
sentences.zh: 我想这导致了一个不可避免的问题，如果他们已经没有几十年了，人们是否觉得是时候离开香港了？

sentences.en: Which I guess leads to the inevitable question, do people feel like it's time to leave Hong Kong if they don't have decades left?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 很多人都考虑过、讨论过。

sentences.en: Many people have thought about it, discuss it.
sentences.zh: 我从认识的每个人那里都听到这种说法。

sentences.en: I hear it from everyone I know.
sentences.zh: 但当然，不是每个人都能说走就走。

sentences.en: But of course, not everyone can just pick up and leave.
sentences.zh: 人们热爱这座城市。

sentences.en: And people love the city.
sentences.zh: 人们不想在温哥华、纽约或伦敦试图重建他们的生活。

sentences.en: People don't want to try to recreate their life here in Vancouver or New York or London.
sentences.zh: 他们希望香港就是他们热爱的那个地方。

sentences.en: They want Hong Kong to be the place that they love.
sentences.zh: 但对他们中的许多人来说，感觉这一切正在迅速消失。

sentences.en: But for many of them, it feels like that that's rapidly disappearing.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀，非常感谢你，在那里注意安全。

sentences.en: Austin, thank you very much and stay safe there.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 周日，佛罗里达州报告了超过15000例新的冠状病毒病例，创下了自大流行开始以来任何州单日最高纪录。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Florida reported more than 15,000 new cases of the coronavirus, marking the highest single-day total in any state since the start of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这波疫情是由佛罗里达州最大城市及其周边地区创纪录的感染率推动的，包括迈阿密、劳德代尔堡、奥兰多和彭萨科拉。

sentences.en: The surge was driven by record infection rates in and around Florida's biggest cities, including Miami, Fort Lauderdale, Orlando, and Pensacola.
sentences.zh: 在迈阿密-戴德县，至少有六家医院已达到满负荷运转。

sentences.en: In Miami-Dade County, at least six hospitals have reached full capacity.
sentences.zh: 在周末，国会民主党人，包括在ABC节目上亮相的众议员亚当·希夫，对特朗普总统决定为他的朋友兼前顾问

sentences.en: And over the weekend, Congressional Democrats, including Representative Adam Schiff on ABC, reacted with fury to President Trump's decision to commute the prison sentence
sentences.zh: 罗杰·斯通减刑的决定感到愤怒。

sentences.en: of his friend and former advisor, Roger Stone.
sentences.zh: 斯通被定罪的部分原因是他对你们的委员会作出了虚假陈述。

sentences.en: Stone was convicted in part for false statements he made to your committee.
sentences.zh: 你对总统有何回应？

sentences.en: What's your response to the president?
sentences.zh: 我认为任何关心这个国家法治的人，都会对总统为蓄意对国会撒谎、

sentences.en: I think anyone who cares about the rule of law in this country is nauseated by the fact that the president has commuted the sentence of someone who willfully lied to Congress,
sentences.zh: 为总统掩盖罪行、恐吓证人、妨碍调查的人减刑这一事实感到恶心。

sentences.en: covered up for the president, intimidated witnesses, obstructed the investigation.
sentences.zh: 斯通原本预计将在几天内向监狱报到，他因妨碍国会对特朗普2016年竞选活动及与俄罗斯可能存在的联系的调查而被定罪。

sentences.en: Stone, who was scheduled to report to prison within days, had been convicted of obstructing a congressional investigation into Trump's 2016 campaign and possible ties to Russia.
sentences.zh: 他撒谎是为了掩盖真相并保护总统。

sentences.en: He lied to cover up and protect the president.
sentences.zh: 而总统通过这次减刑，基本上是在说，如果你为我撒谎，如果你为我掩盖，如果你支持我，

sentences.en: And the president, through this commutation, is basically saying, if you lie for me, if you cover up for me, if you have my back,
sentences.zh: 那么我就会确保你拿到一张免罪金牌。

sentences.en: then I will make sure that you get a get-out-of-jail-free card.
sentences.zh: 两位共和党参议员米特·罗姆尼和帕特·图米与民主党人一起谴责了减刑，罗姆尼称其为一种，引述，

sentences.en: Two Republican senators, Mitt Romney and Pat Toomey, joined Democrats in condemning the commutation, with Romney calling it an act of, quote,
sentences.zh: 前所未有的历史性腐败的行为。

sentences.en: unprecedented historic corruption.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 在本周剩下的时间里，我们将回访我们在大流行初期遇到过的人们，听听自从我们最初的节目播出以来他们发生了什么变化。

sentences.en: For the rest of the week, we're revisiting people we met in the early weeks of the pandemic and hearing what's happened to them since our original episodes first ran.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正准备迎接节假日的聚会客人们。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让您的客人在家中感到自在的秘诀。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？
